claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you find out if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To get started, could you please tell me how many children you would like to claim Child Benefit for, and what are their names?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Yes, I'd like to find out if I'm eligible. I have one child - my son Alex. He's 8 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! It's great to meet you and hear about Alex.

I have a few more questions to help determine your eligibility:

Are you responsible for Alex's care and living expenses? (For example, does Alex live with you?)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, absolutely. Alex lives with me at home and I'm responsible for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Lovely, thank you for confirming that.

Now, could you tell me a bit about your own situation – are you living in the United Kingdom (England, Scotland, Wales, or Northern Ireland)?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK - I'm in Manchester.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great, thank you! Manchester is a lovely city.

One more question: Is Alex currently in full-time education, or if he's not in education, is he under 16 years old?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He's only 8, so he's not 16 yet. He goes to school, obviously - primary school.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect, thank you for confirming that!

Just one more question: Are you (or your spouse/partner, if applicable) receiving any public funds that might affect your immigration status, or do you have any immigration restrictions on your stay in the UK? In other words, are you a UK national, or do you have settled status or the right to live in the UK without restrictions?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm a UK national, so there aren't any immigration restrictions or anything like that.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing all that information. Based on what you've told me, I have everything I need to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

Let me summarise what you've shared:
- You have one child, Alex, who is 8 years old
- Alex lives with you and you are responsible for his care
- You live in Manchester, UK
- Alex is in full-time education (primary school)
- You are a UK national with no immigration restrictions

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great news! Based on the information you've provided, **you are eligible to claim Child Benefit for Alex**.

Here's a summary of why:

✅ **Alex meets the age requirement** – He is 8 years old (under 16)
✅ **You are responsible for Alex** – He lives with you and you are responsible for his care
✅ **You live in the UK** – You reside in Manchester
✅ **You have the right to claim** – As a UK national, you have no immigration restrictions

You can apply for Child Benefit online or by post. If you haven't already claimed, I'd recommend doing so as soon as possible, as Child Benefit can only be backdated for up to 3 months.

Is there anything else you'd like to know about Child Benefit?
